items.title: Louis James Interview, 1959-05-25
items.q: and the violin, I got harmony in Adi Oban. He was a great violin player too.

ctx.x: They keep themselves in practice. Yeah. And they give us-

And that's who Gabriel learned of them. Just like I got the harmony from, and the violin, I got harmony in Adi Oban. He was a great violin player too. Thank you. That was Joe Gabriel, the brother-in-law. Yeah. Yeah. Tennessee Walsh and all that piece of play in my time. Tennessee Walsh. Oh, yeah.
One other man I was going to ask you about, he was more of a boy in your time, Jimmy Noon. Do you remember? Jimmy Noon.
